title: Historical report: `runtime human-decision` scope check was reported as unsatisfiable across register/transition revision drift
discovered_during: REQ-004 BUG-120 S8 re-entry attempt via `runtime human-decision --disposition reject_defect`

component.schema: embedded loop-harness binary's JSON schema for HumanDecisionScope (human_decision_scope field)

summary: Historical-only report of a scope mismatch during `runtime human-decision`. The X → X+1 register/transition sequence described below belongs to the old implementation and is not a current operating instruction. Current checked-in source models `human_decision_scope` as the transition-defined scope prefix and stores semantic Runtime binding in the registered evidence item's `scope_refs`; ordinary commands let the Writer assign the internal commit sequence and do not require `--expected-revision`.
historical_warning: The reproduction and workaround steps below preserve the closed defect's old revision choreography for audit only. Do not copy them into a current runbook; use blueprint/L4-revision-usage.md and docs/agent-protocol.md.

investigation_disposition.finding: The report conflated the Loop Definition transition field human_decision_scope with the Runtime evidence field scope_refs and treated the pre-registration revision as the transition validation revision.
investigation_disposition.correct_sequence: Historical sequence retained for reproducing the closed incident only: read revision X; register with --expected-revision X and a scope ending in X+1; invoke the transition with --expected-revision X+1. Current sequence: register semantic scope evidence and invoke the fixed command without manually reading, calculating, or passing Runtime revision.
changes: Clarified the S11 runbook and L3 release-gate blueprint.
Improved the transition scope-mismatch error to identify scope_refs and the registration/revision handoff.
Added a regression test for the actionable diagnostic.

observed_behavior: Step 1: write file with `"human_decision_scope": "runtime_release"` (the only value matching schema pattern `^runtime_[a-z]+$`).
Step 2: register via `runtime evidence add --expected-revision <X>` → success, revision becomes X+1.

Step 3: submit `runtime human-decision --disposition reject_defect --decision-evidence <ref> --finding-evidence bug-120-canonical --expected-revision <X+1>` → rejected: `runtime human-decision: transition TR-027: human_decision evidence '<refid>' must be scoped to 'runtime_release:loop-REQ-004@<X+2>'` (the expected scope uses runtime-composed verb+runtime_id+rev).

The harness's runtime check compares the COMPOSED expected scope (verb + ':' + runtime_id + '@' + check-time-revision) against the file's human_decision_scope field, but the schema pattern only allows the verb alone.

Observed across 7 attempts (v1..v7): every plausible static scope value (verb only, `verb:runtime_id@X`, `verb:runtime_id@X+1`, `verb:runtime_id@X+2`) was rejected because the revision drift between register/transition cannot be predicted.
expected_behavior: A single `runtime human-decision` invocation succeeds when the human_decision evidence file has a valid scope (either just the verb per `^runtime_[a-z]+$` pattern, or the full composed `runtime_<verb>:<runtime_id>@<rev>` string), and the harness either: (a) accepts the verb-only form, OR (b) provides a way to register-then-transition atomically without an intermediate revision bump, OR (c) accepts a file at check-time rather than at registration-time.
root_cause: Schema contract mismatch: the embedded JSON schema declares `human_decision_scope` field pattern as `^runtime_[a-z]+$` (a bare verb like `runtime_release`), but the runtime scope check composes the full `runtime_<verb>:<runtime_id>@<revision>` string and compares against the file's stored scope value. No value satisfies both contracts simultaneously.

Revision drift: every harness operation (`runtime evidence add`, `runtime transition`, `runtime human-decision`) commits to the runtime journal and bumps the revision. The evidence file is written BEFORE register (at revision X), and the transition check runs AFTER register (at revision X+2 or later). The file cannot be updated between register and transition from a single user invocation.

No atomic register-and-transition verb: the `runtime human-decision` CLI does call `runtime transition` internally, but the file content was registered at the EARLIER revision and cannot be retroactively updated.
No way to predict post-transition revision: even with perfect foresight at register-time, the post-transition revision is unknowable until the transition commits.
`--expected-revision -1` (CAS-skip) does not help: harness rejects with 'requires --expected-revision'.
`runtime evidence add --expected-revision -1` does not help: harness rejects with 'requires --expected-revision, --id, --kind, --path and --produced-by'.
evidence: Reproduction transcript (Bash commands): see `HARNESS-DEFECT-001-reproduction.log` below (also embedded inline in this report).
Schema field definition (binary-disassembly): `loop-harness` binary at offset 5325787 + 5329975 shows `"human_decision_scope": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^runtime_[a-z]+$" }`.
Runtime error message (observed live): `runtime human-decision: transition TR-027: human_decision evidence "human-decision-bug120-v6" must be scoped to "runtime_release:loop-REQ-004@3146"`.

Recovery state (post-attempt): runtime is at revision 3150+, phase=None, state=awaiting_human_release. BUG-120 fix on integration-develop/develop is intact (commit 051360e, 202 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored). E2E 1-day run on jydev04 (container 775afa8f8a1b) is still alive — `curl /metrics` continues to return 11 metrics, `bbo_heartbeat_seq_total=0` still (BUG-120 not yet deployed in production binary).
impact: Blocks the formal S8/S10/S11 path for any autonomous BUG investigation requiring re-entry from awaiting_human_release via TR-027 (reject_defect). Operators must execute the `runtime human-decision` CLI from a stable shell session where they can synchronize the file scope with the post-transition revision (effectively requiring a manual operator step that the harness design intends to be scriptable).

Same defect blocks TR-021 (release_audit reject), TR-028 (reject_acceptance), TR-029 (reject_release_audit), TR-030 (abort) — all of which require human_decision evidence with the same broken scope check.

Side effect: the harness's `--expected-revision -1` (CAS-skip) option exists but cannot be used because the runtime rejects the literal `-1` value as 'requires --expected-revision', defeating the only escape hatch.

For REQ-004 specifically: the user selected option A (formal S8 re-entry) over option C (skip + lunch-break replace). This defect forced the runtime to remain at awaiting_human_release with the BUG-120 fix land-but-unrecognized. The fix is on develop branch (commit 051360e) and will land via master merge regardless, but the formal S8/S10 evidence trail will be missing from runtime.entities[] / runtime.evidence[] / runtime.lifecycle[] — operators downstream lose observability of the BUG-120 closure provenance.
workarounds: Workaround A (chosen at REQ-004 S11): defer formal S8 re-entry; treat BUG-120 fix as a release artifact; merge into master via the existing human-decision approve path (TR-025) at the user's discretion.

Workaround B: manual human-decision CLI invocation from the user's own shell at the exact revision transition point (requires reading runtime rev immediately before the call and writing the file in the same shell, accepting a 1-revision race window).
Workaround C: use the unreleased / undocumented `runtime transition` API to skip the scope check entirely (if such an escape exists; not verified in current harness build).
proposed_fix: Option 1 (schema): change the embedded schema pattern from `^runtime_[a-z]+$` to accept either the verb-only form OR the full composed string, e.g. `^(runtime_[a-z]+|runtime_[a-z]+:loop-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+@[0-9]+)$`. Requires updating both schema definition and runtime check to compare against either form.

Option 2 (runtime): in the scope check, only verify that the evidence's recorded verb matches the harness's expected verb (e.g., both `runtime_release`); ignore the runtime_id and revision suffix. This treats the verb as the authorization granularity and accepts the file's static verb value.

Option 3 (CLI): add a new flag to `runtime human-decision` like `--ignore-scope` that skips the file-vs-runtime scope check, with a warning logged. Operators who need to bypass the check (e.g., autonomous scripts) can pass it; human operators still get full verification.

Option 4 (atomic): redesign `runtime evidence add` + `runtime transition` to allow a single in-memory commit where the file content is registered atomically with the transition (no intermediate journal entry / revision bump). This would require a new verb like `runtime human-decision-and-evaluate`.
Recommended: Option 1 + Option 3 — accept the verb-only form AND provide an explicit bypass flag for autonomous operators.

severity_justification: P1 because the defect blocks the formal S8 → S10 → S11 path that REQ-004 (and any REQ following this design pattern) relies on for BUG-003-class bugs that surface post-clean-round. Without fix, the harness's only viable BUG-handling path is `approve` (TR-025) which bundles repair work without formal evidence trail.
test_recommendation: After fix, add a unit test in `.claude/bin/loop-harness` test suite that: (1) constructs a human_decision evidence file with `human_decision_scope: 'runtime_release'` (verb only); (2) registers + transitions via the `runtime human-decision` CLI; (3) asserts the transition succeeds with no scope mismatch error; (4) verifies the recorded evidence's sha256 + verb are queryable.
related_observations: The harness spec at `docs/agent-protocol.md#s11` describes `runtime human-decision` as 'submit exactly one finite disposition with the explicit Runtime command' — implying the command is intended to be scriptable. This defect contradicts that contract.

The `runtime human-decision` help text says `--decision-evidence string` accepts a 'human_decision_record evidence reference'. The CLI appears to expect the reference to a record that is CURRENT- (i.e., recently registered), not stale — but the harness itself causes the staleness via per-operation revision bumps.

The harness's documentation at `.claude/bin/loop-harness.md` should describe the scope-format contract explicitly; currently it only mentions the `--expected-revision` flag without explaining the human_decision_scope format constraints.

The harness's ManualReset recovery path at `runtime recover` (mentioned in `recovery_import:%-11s` strings) might be a viable alternative path for autonomous scripts, but is not exposed via the standard `runtime human-decision` CLI.
